extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) is a curated subset of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which no prior language model evaluation outperformed the average human-rater score. It contains 6,511 evaluation examples requiring multi-step reasoning, algorithmic reasoning, and natural language understanding, designed to test the limits of large language models.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is a subset of BIG-Bench tasks (23 challenging tasks called BIG-Bench Hard) where prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater. Chain-of-thought prompts were manually composed for each task.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: BIG-Bench evaluation suite tasks, specifically the 23 tasks where language models did not outperform average human-rater performance
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some tasks require knowledge of common practices and presuppositions in Western society, introducing cultural bias toward Western knowledge and perspectives.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses on tasks where prior language models fell short of human-rater performance, and some tasks requiring world knowledge (e.g., Causal Judgement, Ruin Names) remain challenging even with CoT prompting, with no model surpassing human-rater performance on these tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to facilitate research on challenging reasoning tasks for language models, including evaluation and benchmarking of model capabilities using chain-of-thought prompting.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Few-shot chain-of-thought prompting was applied by manually composing three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in BBH, prepending 'let's think step-by-step' to all CoT annotations in the few-shot exemplars.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks were filtered from BIG-Bench to select 23 challenging tasks (BIG-Bench Hard) where prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater. Prompts were strengthened by including task instructions and answer options.

name.evidence: We select a subset of 23 particularly challenging tasks and group them into an evaluation suite referred to as BIG-Bench Hard (BBH), which we make publicly available.

description.evidence: We use the remaining 23 tasks as our curated benchmark that we refer to as BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)... Hence, there are 6,511 evaluation examples in the benchmark in total.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: BIG-Bench (Srivastava et al., 2022) is a diverse evaluation suite that focuses on tasks believed to be beyond the capabilities of current language models... we focus on a suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks which we call BIG-Bench Hard (BBH). rai:dataBiases.evidence: Some BBH tasks require factual and general knowledge about the world as well as the common practices and presuppositions in the Western society... Ruin Names requires knowledge about human perception and usage of humor in the English language as well as the names of artists, bands, and movies in the West.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Causal Judgement and Ruin Names are two tasks on which the performance with CoT prompting is worse—and none of the language models perform better than the average reported human-rater performance.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We release the data and prompts used in the work, as well as the outputs from the Codex models, to facilitate further research.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We manually compose three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in BBH; all the prompts used are shown in Section C. We prepend 'let's think step-by-step' (Kojima et al., 2022) to all CoT annotations in the few-shot exemplars.
